summary: Built in 1920 as a cupola cabin on the Klamath reservation, rebuilt in 1930, and still staffed each summer.

facts.design: cupola cabin (the present building dates from 1930)

access.note: Staffed lookout. The summit road is ungated and drivable, but visitors should approach or climb the tower only when invited by the attendant.

visit.trail_note: Gravel and cinder roads reach the summit, with no gate as of June 2022. Enter or climb only if invited.

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Winema National Forest

events.note: First used as an observation point; a telephone line reached the summit late in the 1919 fire season.
16x16 cabin with a 12x12 glassed tower on the summit, plus a two-room house about 2.5 miles south.
14x20 guard cabin added (a separate building from the lookout).
The first cupola cabin was replaced by the present cupola cabin. The register also gives 1930 as the construction date.
Active each summer from 1931, first by fire guards of the Klamath Tribe.
A July 13, 1939 fire on the Klamath reservation jumped its fire lines and surrounded the butte; on July 14 lookout Frank Coburn said he would not leave his station until he had to.
Lookout passed to the Oregon Department of Forestry (firelookout.com gives 1960; the register describes the state period as running until the mid-1970s).
Added to the National Historic Lookout Register, March 1, 1998.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register's built field says 1920, but its description says the lookout was constructed in 1930. Firelookout.com and the 1920 timber report date the first cabin to 1920 and the present cupola cabin to 1930, so the story gives both dates.

Firelookout.com gives 1960 for the move to the Oregon Department of Forestry. The register says the Indian Agency ran the lookout until about two years before the 1961 Termination Act. The two dates are close, so the story presents them as approximate.
The register gives 6,584 ft (2,007 m); firelookout.com gives 6622 ft and a 2022 trip report gives 6,622 ft. The record keeps the register's figure.

notes_for_editor: The brief's height_m of 4.9 is not supported by any page read, so it is left out of facts; please verify or drop it. Staffing claims come from undated firelookout.com text plus a June 2022 trip report, so the as_of date is the research date. The 1920 and 1930 construction dates conflict in the register and are reconciled in the story. The 2022 trip report is a personal blog and is used only for road and visit conditions. Current 2025-26 staffing was not checked. The 1920 report's 14x20 two-room house and firelookout.com's 14x20 guard cabin (1922) may be the same building; the story reports both as sourced and does not say they differ.
